same_game_correlations.relationship: Team passing yards vs the same team's rushing yards, same game
same_game_correlations.note: The classic game-script negative correlation: a team that runs it well throws it less. A same-team pass-plus-rush prop combination is therefore worth less than the product of its legs.
same_game_correlations.method: Pearson r, Fisher-z 95% CI, two-sided t test

same_game_correlations.relationship: Home passing yards vs away passing yards, same game
same_game_correlations.note: Two quarter-backs in the same game share the same game script, so their passing yards are usually positively correlated, not independent.
same_game_correlations.method: Pearson r, Fisher-z 95% CI, two-sided t test

same_game_correlations.relationship: Home passing yards vs the game total points
same_game_correlations.note: How much of the game total is driven by one team's passing game.
same_game_correlations.method: Pearson r, Fisher-z 95% CI, two-sided t test

same_game_correlations.relationship: Team passing touchdowns vs the same team's rushing touchdowns
same_game_correlations.note: Two scoring props from the same team compete for the same red-zone trips.
same_game_correlations.method: Pearson r, Fisher-z 95% CI, two-sided t test

same_game_correlations.relationship: Game total points vs the closing total line
same_game_correlations.note: How much of the realised total the market line already explains.
same_game_correlations.method: Pearson r, Fisher-z 95% CI, two-sided t test

same_game_correlations.relationship: Top receiver yards vs the second receiver's yards, same team and game
same_game_correlations.note: Target competition inside one passing game. Two receiver overs from the same team are usually negatively correlated.
same_game_correlations.method: Pearson r, Fisher-z 95% CI, two-sided t test

same_game_correlations.relationship: Lead back rushing yards vs the backup's rushing yards, same team and game
same_game_correlations.note: Committee split: the backup's workload rises when the lead back's falls.
same_game_correlations.method: Pearson r, Fisher-z 95% CI, two-sided t test

same_game_correlations.relationship: Quarter-back passing yards vs his top receiver's receiving yards, same team and game
same_game_correlations.note: The single most common same-game prop pairing. A strong positive correlation means the parlay is worth MORE than the product of its legs, which is why books price these specially.
same_game_correlations.method: Pearson r, Fisher-z 95% CI, two-sided t test
